previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for initiation of hemodialysis due to worsening uremic symptoms including fatigue, nausea, confusion, and dizziness. She has end-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive chronic kidney disease and type 1 diabetes with gastroparesis and autonomic neuropathy. Hemodialysis was successfully initiated using her left arm AV fistula, though a subsequent fistulogram and angioplasty were required to address access difficulty. During the procedure, she experienced a brief episode of paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia that resolved spontaneously. Orthostatic hypotension persisted despite dialysis and was managed with fludrocortisone and IV fluids, with improvement. Her shortness of breath was attributed to deconditioning and orthostasis, with normal oxygenation and imaging. She was discharged home stable, with ongoing dialysis planned, fludrocortisone for orthostasis, and instructions to use a walker for safety.

uncomplicated, please see associated operative report for 
further details. In the PACU her dressing over the peritoneal 
dialysis catheter was noted to be saturated with blood 
approximately 1.5 hours post operatively. After it was taken 
down there was active oozing coming from the catheter exit site

after which time the bleeding stop and her dressing was 
replaced. Also while in the PACU her oxygen saturation would 
intermittently drop to the ___ on room air and resolved 
spontaneously when she was encouraged to take deep breaths. 
Nasal cannula oxygen was applied and she was admitted overnight

medications were restarted. Incentive spirometery use was 
encouaged and her pain was controlled with the use of vicodin.

subsequently discharged home and will follow up in ___
